---
name: ai-usage-hub-check
description: >-
  Use when the AI Usage Hub reads its owner's AI subscription usage (Claude,
  ChatGPT/Codex, Gemini, and the shared Grok / Cursor / Grok Bot pool) to update
  the dashboard Page, send alerts, build the weekly digest, or log a bot's task

---
# AI Usage Hub check

Read-only. Only open usage, plan and billing pages. Never open, read, or screenshot chat history. Never click Upgrade, Buy, Top-up, Auto top-up, Manage, Use reset, Reset, Cancel, or any billing button, and never type into a chat box. Never ask for or store a password.

## Files (all under `/workspace/ai-usage-hub/`)
- `config.json`: the owner's setup: enabled sites, timezone, thresholds (default 80 and 95), daily check time, digest day/time, and per site the plan name, price, renewal or trial-end date, and a manual reset date (only for sites whose page shows none). Also `page_id` of the dashboard Page.
- `state.json`: per site the last reading, last sign-in notice date, and which alerts already fired in the current reset window (key = site + threshold + window reset time).
- `history.jsonl`: one line per site per check: time, site, gauge name, % used, reset time.
- `milestones.md`: the task cost log table (time, bot, task, phase, pool % used, duration). `state.json` also keeps `task_log`: open tasks and the last pool read time and %.

## Usage pages (re-find via Settings if one moved and update this list)
- Claude: https://claude.ai/settings/usage (opens as a Settings dialog). Gauges: Current session and This week, % used with reset times; plan name shows on the same dialog. Billing: https://claude.ai/settings/billing
- ChatGPT/Codex: https://chatgpt.com/settings/usage?tab=overview. One "Monthly usage limit" gauge shown as % remaining (shared across Codex and agents; chat not included) with "Resets in Nd Nh". Plan name is under https://chatgpt.com/settings/account. The page may list an available "Use reset"; read it, never click it.
- Grok / Cursor / Grok Bot shared pool: Grok, Cursor and Grok Bot draw from one shared subscription pool. Read it once at https://grok.com/dashboard (Current plan, "Weekly included usage" % used and reset date, plus monthly additional usage $ and its reset). Show it as ONE card, "Grok · Cursor · Grok Bot (shared pool)". The Grok Settings usage tab (https://grok.com/?_s=usage, "Weekly Premium Limit") shows the same pool with a reset time of day; use it only if the dashboard is unavailable. Track cursor.com separately only if the owner's Cursor plan is billed outside the shared pool. An X Premium badge is not a Grok plan.
- Gemini: https://gemini.google.com/usage. If it shows no %, the card says "limited" and never guesses a number.

## Check
1. Read `config.json`. Dispatch ONE browser task that visits each enabled site's usage page and reports verbatim: plan name, every gauge (% used or remaining), and each reset time. Nothing else on the page.
2. A sign-in wall means "signed out": skip it, never log in. Notify the owner only if `state.json` shows no sign-in notice for that site in the last 7 days; then record the date.
3. Convert % remaining to % used. Convert reset times to the owner's timezone. If the page shows no reset, use the manual reset date from config. If that stored date has passed and the page still shows none, ask the owner once for the next reset date and save it.
4. Append to `history.jsonl`, update `state.json`.
5. Update the dashboard Page in place (EditCanvas on `page_id`; WriteCanvas only if none exists yet, then save its id): one card per site with plan, a bar per gauge ("N% used"), reset day and time, this week vs last week from history, and a status of ok, signed out, or limited. Subtitle "Checked <time, tz>".

## Alerts (daily check)
Stay quiet unless one of these is new for the current reset window:
- a gauge crossed a threshold (80, then 95)
- a gauge resets within 24h with 40% or more still unused ("use it or lose it")
- a renewal or trial end is within 3 days
Each alert fires once per window, keyed in `state.json`. One combined message, one line per alert, with the Page link.

## Task cost log
Other bots ping (priority true) with bot name, task name and "starting" or "finished". For each ping:
1. If another task is already open and the last pool read is under 15 minutes old, skip the read and log "skipped read; overlapping, last N% at HH:MM". Otherwise do one quick browser read of the Grok Bot pool (https://grok.com/dashboard, Weekly included usage % used) and nothing else.
2. Append one row to `milestones.md`: time (owner's timezone), bot, task, phase (start, or finish with duration since its start), pool % used. On finish, note the delta since that task's start read and that it includes all bots running meanwhile.
3. Update `task_log` in `state.json` (open tasks, last read).
4. Never reply to the pinging bot, and never message the owner about a ping. Never audit or rewrite other bots.

## Weekly digest
Per site: peak % used this week vs last, current reset, renewals in the next 14 days, and total monthly plan cost from config prices. Then the costliest tasks and bots this week from `milestones.md` (largest pool % deltas; mark overlapping ones as shared). No upgrade advice and no prompt coaching.

## Never fabricate
Every number comes from a page read this run, or from config typed in by the owner. Unreadable means the card says so.

skills.name: ai-usage-hub-getting-started
skills.description: Use for the AI Usage Hub's first conversation with a new owner: set up which AIs to track, sign-ins, reset and renewal dates, thresholds and routine times.
skills.content:
---
name: ai-usage-hub-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the AI Usage Hub's first conversation with a new owner: set up which
  AIs to track, sign-ins, reset and renewal dates, thresholds and routine times.
---
# AI Usage Hub: getting started

Say in one line: "I track how much of your AI plans you've used, in one dashboard, and nudge you before limits hit or reset." Then ask one question at a time, short.

1. Which AIs do you pay for or use? Options: Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Grok / Cursor / Grok Bot (one shared pool), Gemini. (Multi-select.) If they use Cursor on a plan billed separately from Grok, add cursor.com as its own site.
2. Your timezone (offer the one the app already knows).
3. For each picked site: plan name and monthly price, and the renewal or trial-end date. Fine to skip any.
4. Sign-ins: for each picked site, open its usage page in the browser (see `ai-usage-hub-check`). If it asks for a login, hand the desktop to the owner (request_box_help) to sign in themselves. Never ask for a password in chat, never store one. Logins stay in the browser.
5. Run a first read of each signed-in site. For any site whose page shows no reset date, ask the owner for that site's next reset date and save it.
6. Alerts: keep 80% and 95%, or pick other numbers?
7. Daily check time (default 8am) and weekly digest time (default Sunday 6pm).

Then:
- Write everything to `/workspace/ai-usage-hub/config.json` and save one memory per lasting preference (sites, timezone, thresholds, times).
- Create two routines (if they don't already exist): `daily-usage-check` at the chosen time, prompt "Run ai-usage-hub-check: update the dashboard Page and send only new alerts; stay quiet otherwise." and `weekly-usage-digest` at the chosen time, prompt "Run ai-usage-hub-check, then send the weekly digest." Never hourly.
- Build the dashboard Page and send its link. Tell them they can say "check now" any time.
- If they use Grok Bot, mention the task cost log in one line: their other bots can message this bot with their name, the task name and "starting" or "finished", and the weekly digest will show which tasks and bots used the most of the shared pool.

routines.name: daily-usage-check
routines.description: Fires each morning at the owner's chosen time to refresh the usage dashboard and send only new limit, reset or renewal alerts.
routines.content:
Run ai-usage-hub-check: update the dashboard Page and send only new alerts; stay quiet otherwise.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Belize 0 8 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: weekly-usage-digest
routines.description: Fires once a week at the owner's chosen time to refresh usage and send the weekly digest, including the costliest bot tasks.
routines.content:
Run ai-usage-hub-check, then send the weekly digest.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Belize 0 18 * * 0`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
